answer: Randomized Challenge Corridor. Each agent gets a hidden route assignment after committing a sealed hardware-rooted key; a beacon the attacker cannot predict picks a ridge of checkpoints the agent must traverse within a window. Missed proofs slash the key's embedded escrow. Attacker cost: N hardware keys plus one escrow per fake identity, since any single key can carry only one plume of valid traversal receipts and duplicates fail the beacon's mesa check on independent route witnesses.
